published commands and completed reference earn four configuration goals, with real echo required for all eight tasks
matching-prefix AD 10 backups remain configured but inactive while all four AD 1 primaries forward directly
primary failure withdraws both directions, installs four AD 10 backups, carries real traffic through R2 and automatically recovers
shutting the far end of the primary link also drives real bidirectional IPv4 and IPv6 failover and restoration
a missing return backup breaks only its address family during failure despite the correctly installed forward backup
equal AD is not a floating backup, and AD 255 never supplies connectivity after the primary disappears
a more-specific host route preempts the primary by prefix length and cannot earn the matching-network floating-route task
an incorrectly scoped IPv6 backup cannot earn credit or deliver after primary failure, while the IPv4 backup still works
losing both paths stops remote traffic; restoring the primary repairs it without inventing another backup
untracked static primaries do not withdraw merely because an otherwise-up direct link drops packets
all published verification commands work on primary and backup paths, including actual traceroutes and route/config distance differences
saved reload rebuilds active floating routes during a failed primary, and startup reboot restores the saved preferred path and progress
verificationNotes: The guide has four live configuration goals and four retained echo observations. Its failure/recovery exercise requires repeating route lookups, real traffic and traceroutes in both states; configuration goals require restored primaries at completion.
The completed reference contains four configuration goals with no fabricated traffic credit. All eight tasks require four actual echo tests.

All primary/backup pairs match the same prefix. AD 10 backups stay configured but inactive while the AD 1 primary is installed; local primary-link failure installs AD 10 in both directions and recovery automatically reinstalls AD 1.

Ethernet routes specify exit interface plus next hop. Link-local IPv6 addresses are interface-scoped. The lab tests local link failure; it does not claim remote-reachability monitoring without IP SLA or tracking.
Configured backup scoring is independent of current installation. A missing return backup, wrong prefix, wrong distance or wrong IPv6 interface cannot earn the required backup goal.
Browser test profiles and their local file URLs are isolated per theme/viewport. Startup storage and toast diagnostics are retained on a failed reload.

Overlapping file-based Chrome runs intermittently reopened with empty localStorage before application code. Their saved documents replayed correctly with active AD 10 routes and six completed goals; twelve consecutive isolated browser reloads also passed. File scenarios are now serialized and use fresh persistent profiles. Five successful viewport/theme runs are retained, with the failed dark-320 case rerun in isolation. This changes the QA harness, not application storage or simulation logic.

All six complete viewport/theme workflows and both permalink checks passed across the recorded runs; successful unchanged cases were retained and the failed case alone was rerun. Seven general catalog checks also passed. Final root/dist HTML and every frozen browser input match byte for byte. Light desktop topology and light/dark 320px guides were visually reviewed.
scope: Adds a focused dual-stack Floating Static Route catalog lab, guide resources, completed reference, documentation and regression/browser coverage. Uses the existing IPv4/IPv6 forwarding, route selection and lesson criteria. No simulation engine, terminal, theme, dependency or backend changes. No live CML validation is claimed.
